report.summary: Reviewed mint.py chunk 3 of 3: verified mint_task_from_landed_edit, mint_from_commit, confirm_task, load/save/add/confirm_minted_tasks against docstrings; claims mostly kept, some uncheckable.
risks: mint_from_commit | medium | rename handling: uses last path for 'after' but does not read 'before' from the rename source, so a renamed file's diff may be empty or wrong; settle by checking git diff-tree output for rename rows in a test fixture.
load_minted_tasks | medium | unguarded t['id'] in sort key raises KeyError on malformed store entries; settle by inspecting the store schema and adding a robustness test.

confirm_minted_task | medium | mutates tasks list in place; if confirm_task returns early (non-quarantine), save still rewrites the store; settle by reading whether that is intended and adding a test for non-quarantine id.
mint_task_from_landed_edit | low | if sha is None, before is None for all files and diff is against empty; docstring assumes HEAD exists; settle by checking caller guarantees a valid repo.
mint_from_commit | low | if parent is None (root commit), before is None for all files, diff is against empty; docstring implies this is intended; settle by reading the --root comment.
add_minted_task | low | idempotence depends on _mint_from_diffs hash stability; settle by reading _mint_from_diffs in earlier chunk.
todos: Verify rename handling in mint_from_commit with a real git rename fixture.
Add a test for load_minted_tasks with a malformed store entry (missing 'id').
Add a test for confirm_minted_task with a non-quarantine task id.
Confirm that _mint_from_diffs handles files dict entries where both before and after are None.

handoff.purpose: Review the public minting entry points and persistence/confirmation helpers against their docstrings.

symbols.name: _log_mint_diagnostics
symbols.note: Logs skipped out-of-scope files and no-task reason via _LOG.info.

symbols.name: mint_task_from_landed_edit
symbols.note: Mints a task from report['wrote'] by diffing HEAD vs worktree; returns None if no writes or no cross-file diff.

symbols.name: mint_from_commit
symbols.note: Mints a task from a git commit via diff-tree --root; returns list with zero or one task.

symbols.name: confirm_task
symbols.note: Increments confirmations in place; promotes tier to primary at threshold; no-op for non-quarantine.

symbols.name: load_minted_tasks
symbols.note: Reads JSON store, returns sorted list by id, or [] if missing.

symbols.name: save_minted_tasks
symbols.note: Overwrites store with schema 1, sorted tasks by id, deterministic formatting.

symbols.name: add_minted_task
symbols.note: Idempotently upserts a task by id into the store.

symbols.name: confirm_minted_task
symbols.note: Loads store, confirms one task by id, persists, returns updated task or None.

claims.text: A task that DID mint carries its own skipped_out_of_scope/must_include_dropped fields; this is what surfaces the same information -- and the no-task-minted reason -- for the cases where there is no task dict to carry it.
claims.why: The function reads diagnostics['skipped_out_of_scope'] and diagnostics['reason'] and logs them; the task dict construction above includes skipped_out_of_scope and must_include_dropped fields.

claims.text: report['wrote'] IS disk_changed from offload.py:194-197 -- the files that ACTUALLY changed on disk, found by diffing a before/after content-hash snapshot taken around the run.
claims.why: The claim references offload.py internals and a snapshot mechanism not present in this chunk; this chunk only reads report.get('wrote').

claims.text: the model's self-reported files_changed is deliberately not read, for the same reason offload.py itself refuses to trust it for the write-mode gate.
claims.why: The function only reads report.get('wrote'); it never accesses files_changed.

claims.text: The edit is assumed uncommitted (offload writes straight into the working tree and never commits): 'before' is read from git HEAD, 'after' from the file currently on disk.
claims.why: The code uses _resolve_sha(repo_root, 'HEAD') and _show(repo_root, 'HEAD', rel) for before, and _read_worktree(repo_root, rel) for after.

claims.text: A file the run created has no HEAD blob (before = None); a file it deleted has nothing left on disk (after = None).
claims.why: before is set to _show(...) if sha is truthy, otherwise None; after is _read_worktree(...), which presumably returns None for missing files (consistent with the code).

claims.text: Returns None if there is nothing to mint: no writes reported, every write's content is symbol-identical to HEAD (e.g. a formatting-only touch this diff granularity can't see through), no written file is in the project's index scope, or only one in-scope file has a diffed symbol (no cross-file label exists -- see the module docstring's CROSS-FILE ONLY rule).
claims.why: The function returns None only when disk_changed is empty; the other conditions (symbol-identical, out-of-scope, single-file) are handled inside _mint_from_diffs, which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Currently mints a single aggregate task per commit (via the same _mint_from_diffs used for landed edits); returns a list so a future split (e.g. one task per hunk, for very large commits) is additive rather than a signature change.
claims.why: The function calls _mint_from_diffs once and returns [task] if task else [].

claims.text: Returns [] for an unresolvable ref, a commit that touches no in-scope file, or one where only a single in-scope file has a diffed symbol (no cross-file label exists) -- never raises.
claims.why: The unresolvable-ref case is handled (returns [] if _resolve_sha fails); the other cases are decided inside _mint_from_diffs, which is not in this chunk. The 'never raises' claim is also uncheckable because _git, _show, and _in_scope_modules are not shown.

claims.text: --root: a commit with no parent (the very first commit of history) is diffed against the empty tree instead of silently producing no rows. No-op for every other commit (it already has a parent to diff against).
claims.why: The code passes --root to diff-tree; parent is resolved as full_sha^, which is None for a root commit, and before is set to None in that case, effectively diffing against empty.

claims.text: Promotes task['tier'] from 'quarantine' to 'primary' once confirmations reaches MINT_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD.
claims.why: The code increments confirmations and sets tier to 'primary' when confirmations >= MINT_CONFIRM_THRESHOLD.

claims.text: A no-op on a task that is not currently quarantined: a primary task doesn't need more confirming, and 'confirming' a hand_reachable task is meaningless -- it was never gated in the first place.
claims.why: The function returns the task unchanged if tier != 'quarantine'.

claims.text: Returns the same (mutated) dict for convenient chaining; callers that need the pre-mutation task should copy it first.
claims.why: The function mutates and returns the same dict object.

claims.text: Read the persisted mint store, or [] if it does not exist yet.
claims.why: The function returns [] if os.path.exists(p) is false.

claims.text: This is the ONLY load path by which a minted task can reach daedalus.eval.harness.all_tasks() and therefore any go/no-go number -- without it, mint_task_from_landed_edit/mint_from_commit produced dicts that lived only as long as the caller's local variable.
claims.why: The claim concerns harness.all_tasks() and other load paths in the codebase; not observable in this chunk.

claims.text: Sorted by id for deterministic iteration (PYTHONHASHSEED-independent), matching the rest of this repo's output-determinism rule.
claims.why: The function returns sorted(data.get('tasks', []), key=lambda t: t['id']).

claims.text: Overwrite the mint store with exactly tasks. Deterministic formatting (sorted keys, sorted by id) so the diff is meaningful in review -- same contract as harness.write_baseline.
claims.why: The function writes json.dump with sort_keys=True and indent=2, and sorts tasks by id. The reference to harness.write_baseline is not verifiable here but the deterministic formatting claim is satisfied.

claims.text: Returns the path written.
claims.why: The function returns p.

claims.text: Persist task into the mint store, keyed by id. Idempotent: minting the same diff twice (same target + same must_include, via the content hash in _mint_from_diffs) yields the same id and overwrites in place rather than duplicating -- re-running a mint (e.g. after a rebase that reproduces an identical patch) must not inflate the quarantine count.
claims.why: The function builds a dict keyed by task['id'] and overwrites any existing entry with the same id before saving. The id-hash part is in _mint_from_diffs, but the overwrite behavior is as claimed.

claims.text: Load the store, confirm ONE task by id (see confirm_task), persist the mutation, and return the updated task -- or None if task_id is not in the store.
claims.why: The function loads tasks, iterates to find the matching id, calls confirm_task on it, saves, and returns the task; returns None if not found.

claims.text: The only durable way a quarantined mint accumulates confirmations and eventually promotes to primary; confirm_task alone only mutates an in-memory dict that would otherwise evaporate.
claims.why: confirm_task alone does not persist; confirm_minted_task saves the store after confirming. Whether it is the only durable way is uncheckable, but the persistence behavior is as claimed.

observations.what: mint_from_commit uses the last path in a diff-tree line as 'after' but reads 'before' from the same path; for a rename (status R), 'before' should come from the source path, which is the second-to-last field. This could produce an empty diff for renames.
load_minted_tasks sorts by t['id'] without guarding against missing 'id'; a malformed store entry would raise KeyError, contradicting the 'never raises' spirit and the docstring's simple contract.
confirm_minted_task mutates the tasks list in place and saves even if confirm_task was a no-op (non-quarantine task), causing an unnecessary store rewrite.
mint_task_from_landed_edit sets before=None when sha is falsy, meaning it diffs against empty; the docstring assumes HEAD exists, but the code gracefully degrades.

mint_from_commit sets before=None when parent is None (root commit), so the diff is against empty; the comment says this is intended, but it also means a root commit that adds a single file will mint a task even though there is no cross-file diff.
